subject: Pricing path for VPC / on-prem: fees, tiers, and discount request
messages:
From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme-logistics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-logistics.com
Date: Sun, 28 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC/on-prem pricing and support tiers — info request

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme Logistics is interested in a private deployment (VPC) for our core routing and TMS features. Procurement asked me to get a clear commercial picture so we can move to an internal approval:

- What is Redwood's recommended licensing model for VPC/on-prem (seat-based? capacity commit? per-token uplift?).
- What are the platform fees vs. per-instance license fees? Any minimums?
- Support tiers and SLAs (Standard vs. Enterprise) — who handles patching and security patches in a VPC?
- Do you offer multi-year discounts or migration credits for an on-prem migration?

We have a tough fiscal window; customers of our size typically need a ~25% discount on list for a 2-year commitment. Can you share an indicative commercial? If it helps, I can route a procurement template or draft SOW.

Thanks,
Maria Garcia
Director, Digital Platforms
Acme Logistics

[Signature block]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Sep 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC/on-prem pricing and support tiers — info request

Maria — great to hear. High-level answers below; I can follow with a formal written proposal and three attachments (SOW, license matrix, SOC2 summary) if that works.

Short answers:
- Licensing model: primary commercial is a reserved-capacity + platform fee. Customers commit to a baseline GPU capacity (monthly vCPUs/GPU-equivalent) and pay a platform/managed-service fee that covers control plane, upgrade tooling, and observability. There is an optional per-token add-on for burst usage.
- Platform fee: tiered by deployment size. For customers at Acme's quoted qps, the platform fee minimum is typically $35k/month.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours, ticketed), Business (24x5, faster P1), Enterprise (24x7, on-call + named CS). For VPC, Redwood supports the control plane and coordinates patch windows; on-prem components (if fully air-gapped) can be covered under Enterprise with a managed-services engagement.
- Discounts: we do multi-year and commit-based discounts; typical ranges are 10–30% depending on term and committed capacity. Migration credits can be structured but require an attached SOW for the professional services piece.

I will loop Laura (sales lead) and Priyom (pricing/solutions) to get a formal price ladder. Do you have an internal procurement template we should fill, or should I send our standard SOW/license matrix?

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment stub: none in this message]
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: VPC/on-prem pricing and support tiers — Acme request

Team — forwarding Acme's ask. Quick context: Acme is a mid-market logistics customer with potential for expansion to Dedicated and a future Private on-prem rollout. Maria asked explicitly for ~25% off list for a 2-year commit. Ben, what's our baseline here? Priyom — can you propose a commercial ladder we can present (list, 1-year, 2-year, 3-year) and call out which line items are non-negotiable (platform minimum, security add-ons)?

I'd prefer to keep migration credits limited to professional services hours (no shadow credits). For support, Acme will likely want Enterprise if they require Redwood-managed patches. If we reduce platform fee to hit their target discount, we'll need a 24-month commit and a partial prepay.

Can you draft options (A/B/C) so we can fast-turn to Maria?

- Laura
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Oct 2025 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: VPC/on-prem pricing and support tiers — Acme request

Laura / Ben — draft pricing ladders below (high-level). Numbers are placeholders until Ben confirms expected committed GPU equivalent and qps.

Option A (Conservative) — 12-month commitment
- Platform fee: $35k/month
- Reserved capacity license: $18k/month (baseline GPUs)
- Support: Business tier $6k/month
- Total list: $59k/month ($708k/yr)
- Discount ability: up to 12% on list for 12-month with 30% prepaid

Option B (Recommended) — 24-month commitment (offers best balance)
- Platform fee: $30k/month (5k reduction w/ term)
- Reserved capacity license: $17k/month
- Support: Enterprise tier $10k/month (managed patches + named CS)
- Total list: $57k/month ($684k/yr)
- Discount ability: up to 20% with 24-month commit and 50% prepaid + migration credits limited to 80 PS hours

Option C (Aggressive) — 36-month strategic commit
- Platform fee: $28k/month
- Reserved capacity license: $16k/month
- Support: Enterprise $10k/month
- Total list: $54k/month ($648k/yr)
- Discount ability: up to 28% with 36-month commit and full prepay; migration credits negotiable

Notes:
- Minimum platform fee floor = $25k/month for any term; below that we cannot guarantee capacity isolation guarantees.
- SOC2 and audit assistance included for Enterprise.
- Any customer-requested on-site work billed as PS.

Ben — if Acme is asking for ~25% off, Option B with 20% + $20k PS credit might get them there but requires 50% prepay. Thoughts?

-Priyom
Lead, Solutions Pricing
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Oct 2025 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial options (A/B/C) and next steps — Acme Logistics

Maria — attaching the SOW, license matrix and a SOC2 summary per your request. Below are our three commercial options; I pulled Option B forward as the recommended starting point based on size.

(Attachments: RDW_SOW_v2.pdf, license_matrix.xlsx, SOC2_summary.pdf)

Summary (condensed):
- Option A (12m) — list $59k/mo; max 12% discount with 30% prepay
- Option B (24m) — list $57k/mo; up to 20% discount with 50% prepay + 80 PS hours migration credit (we can structure $20k in credits against first-year invoices)
- Option C (36m) — list $54k/mo; up to 28% discount with full prepay; migration credits adjustable

We are willing to move on the platform fee to help reach your internal target. To get to ~25% off list, we'd need at least Option B with 50% prepay and acceptance of a 24-month committed capacity. I can put pricing in HubSpot once you confirm which option looks best and whether procurement prefers a 2- or 3-year term.

Next steps:
1) Maria: tell us which option aligns with Acme's procurement window (12/24/36 months).
2) If 24m preferred, we'll prepare an official quote + term sheet and a statement of work with the PS hours.
3) If you need procurement-specific fields filled, attach your template and we'll populate it.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call to go through numbers if helpful.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment stubs: RDW_SOW_v2.pdf (PDF, 112KB), license_matrix.xlsx (Excel, 48KB), SOC2_summary.pdf (PDF, 92KB)]
From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acme-logistics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-logistics.com
Date: Thu, 2 Oct 2025 16:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commercial options (A/B/C) and next steps — Acme Logistics

Ben — thanks for the fast turnaround and the attachments. Procurement prefers Option B but needs a clean path to 25% off list without full 50% prepay. Two asks: 

1) Can we move to 45% prepay instead of 50% and get the 20% discount + an additional $10k PS credit to effectively reach ~25% net?
2) Please confirm that Enterprise support includes scheduled patch windows coordinated with Acme and a monthly security review. 

If you can confirm those two items in writing, I will route to our CFO and legal for an internal approval. Could you also include a short term-sheet that legal can use to begin redlines?

Appreciate it — Maria
Director, Digital Platforms
Acme Logistics
[Procurement note: target committee review week of Oct 13]
